clue.text: Spy a refined sort of chap?

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a refined sort of man

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a secret operative is really a well-bred fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy is a secret operative working for a government or organisation.

clue.text: Get into a boil about ban

indicators.note: about signals that the words before it are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets furious over a prohibition imposed on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link; 'about' rearranges INTO A BOIL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the formal ending or outlawing of something, as a ban does.

clue.text: Watches locomotive that has trouble with lamps

parts.note: watches as a noun-like verb: eyes means watches
a locomotive pulls a train

explanation.surface: Someone observes an engine that is having problems with its lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamps' is old slang for the eyes, so the definition is fair; 'that has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain or fatigue of the organs of sight, which slang calls lamps.

clue.text: Knock back some of the gin

indicators.note: to knock back is to drive backwards, so the word for some is read in reverse

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Someone downs a portion of their gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests drinking, but it reverses PART; gin here is a snare, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, so it is a device of capture.

clue.text: Four-letter word that upsets Margaret T

indicators.note: upsets means knocks over, so the letters of the name and initial are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude expletive offends a woman called Margaret T, perhaps Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests a swear word, but here it is literal. 'Upsets' rearranges MARGARET into ETRAGRAM, placed after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek tetra, four, plus gramma, letter: a word of exactly four characters.

clue.text: New tan carpets for restaurant, by the way

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the following letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh tan floor coverings are ordered for an eating place.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'can', but only 'tan' gives the right letters: TAN CARPETS FOR rearranged. 'By the way' is part of the definition, meaning beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A British roadside eatery for lorry drivers, so a diner by the highway.

clue.text: A boundary put up in league

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written from bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: a six is a cricket boundary hit over the rope without bouncing

explanation.surface: A border is erected within an alliance of territories.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball hit over the boundary rope scores six.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, a league of nations.

clue.text: Old money one charges in Africa

definitions.meaning: an African animal known for charging at threats

explanation.surface: Inherited wealth is compared with something that rushes at you on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for cash, and a horned beast that charges on the savannah.

clue.text: Giant figure makes Mum curious

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mother
agog means eagerly curious

explanation.surface: A huge statue arouses a mother's curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giant figures, guardians of the City of London, kept at the Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a pair of legendary giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.

clue.text: Cockney's comic artist is at Covent Garden

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial aitch of words

parts.note: Bob Hope was a famous comedian
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A London-accented comedian or painter turns up in Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is home to London's Royal Opera House, so what is at Covent Garden is the art form performed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House stands in Covent Garden, so dramatic sung works are staged there.

clue.text: Ropy way of letting oneself down

definitions.text: Ropy way of letting oneself down

parts.words: Ropy way of letting oneself down
parts.note: ropy suggests poor quality and letting oneself down suggests a disappointment, but read literally it is a descent by rope

explanation.definitionFit: A climber's method of descending a cliff face on a doubled rope.

clue.text: One keeps records of ground-rents

parts.note: ground-rents suggests property fees, but read as rents in the ground it means earthquake tears

explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who records earth tremors, the tears in the earth, on instruments.

clue.text: Has a little Greek

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: A jot or tiny quantity, and the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Up and about in a shake

parts.note: to stir is to shake up or agitate

explanation.surface: Someone is up and moving, all in a tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means out of bed and moving around.

clue.text: Air of boy starting geometry

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of the word geometry

explanation.surface: A lad has the look of someone just beginning maths lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like atmosphere or demeanour; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or tune.

clue.text: Gleaming silver brassed off?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
brassed off is British slang for fed up, which is low in spirits

explanation.surface: Polished silverware has had the brass rubbed off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brassed off' is British slang for annoyed or fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means glowing or shining.

clue.text: Lower half of dining-room for curry

indicators.note: in a down entry, the lower half is the second five letters of the ten

explanation.surface: The bottom part of a dining area is set aside for a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like food; it is the verb meaning to brush down a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to brush and tend its coat, which is what a stable hand does.

clue.text: Non-racial game, perhaps, of transatlantic relations?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A sport free of racial division might be a symbol of US-UK friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing dealings between Britain and the United States across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Cereals so wrong in a covered oven-dish

indicators.note: wrong means incorrectly placed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breakfast grains were mistakenly put into a lidded baking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep lidded pot for slow baking in the oven, and the stew cooked in it.

clue.text: He believed he was winning on the pools

definitions.text: He believed he was winning on the pools

parts.words: He believed he was winning on the pools
parts.note: winning on the pools suggests a football betting win, but here winning means charming, as seen in a reflection in pools of water

explanation.definitionFit: The youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection in a pool.

clue.text: What doctors say can not be passed on, touchingly

definitions.text: What doctors say can not be passed on, touchingly

parts.words: What doctors say can not be passed on, touchingly
parts.note: a medical verdict that a disease cannot spread through physical contact

explanation.definitionFit: Describing an illness that does not spread by physical contact between people.

clue.text: River trial

definitions.meaning: a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing

explanation.definitionFit: The Test is a Hampshire river, and an exam or trial of something.

clue.text: It must be turned over on the tenth

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece
turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Something has to be flipped on the tenth day of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tenth part of one's yearly income given to the church.

clue.text: Fish used to stink

definitions.meaning: the past tense of a verb for giving off a strong odour

explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery fish, and the British past tense of the verb meaning to give off an odour.

clue.text: Precocious little girl who could go either way?

indicators.note: reads the same forwards or backwards, so the word can be read either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A cheeky young girl might turn out good or bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could go either way' sounds like uncertainty but means the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward, cheeky girl who acts older than her years is called a little madam.

clue.text: House found in home counties, by motorway

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east, SE
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A dwelling is located near London, next to a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; the M1 is a main motorway north from London.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached home, sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Mount wrapped in blanket, Naturally

indicators.note: wrapped in means the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A horse is draped in a rug as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a horse; it is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, a mountain.

clue.text: Employed editor to support you and me?

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: us means you and me

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a newspaper boss was hired to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means employed in the sense of put to use.

clue.text: As score came up, it went the wrong way

indicators.note: wrong way means the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: When the result was announced, things went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so the one arriving as the score is reached is the ordinal for that number.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so the item reached when the count hits a score holds that ordinal place.

clue.text: Stays, the highest on board?

definitions.meaning: read as S plus tops, the topmost parts, as on a ship's masts

explanation.definitionFit: Halts or stays put; also playfully the topmost points aboard a ship.

clue.text: Fan of former farm-vehicle

parts.note: ex means former
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast of an old farm machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an enthusiast; it is a device that draws out air.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventilating device that draws stale air out of a room.

clue.text: Grounds, for example, held by doctors

indicators.note: held by means placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Reasons, for instance, are kept by medical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons; it is the sediment left in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are sediment left at the bottom, the residue.
